extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, and OED/USPTO staff
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, duties, and procedural requirements applicable to a registered patent practitioner who has been suspended for misconduct, including the sanction, reporting, notice, affidavit, reinstatement, and probation rules under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60. Covers what must be done during suspension and conditions for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction for disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes statutory and regulatory authority for OED/USPTO to adjudicate practitioner misconduct and enter Final Orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Committing a criminal act that reflects adversely on the practitioner's honesty, trustworthiness or fitness as a practitioner in other respects (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent acknowledged committing Assault in the Fourth Degree (Wash. Rev. Code § 9A.36.041) which constitutes misconduct under this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length of suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be suspended from practice before the Office in patent matters for six months commencing on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific sanction imposed by Final Order; sets the baseline period during which respondent may not practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing to file petition for reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may file a petition with the OED Director seeking reinstatement two months after the date the Final Order is signed, provided he is otherwise in compliance with the terms and conditions of the Agreement and Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although a petition may be filed after two months, respondent remains suspended until reinstatement is granted pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to remain suspended until formal reinstatement order
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall remain suspended from practice before the USPTO until the OED Director grants a petition requesting Respondent's reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a petition does not automatically end the suspension; formal grant is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation following reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall serve a two-year probationary period commencing on the date of an order granting his reinstatement to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probationary conditions described in the Final Order and subject to monitoring and enforcement procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly reporting during suspension and probation
rubrics_metrics.description: While suspended and during his probationary period, Respondent shall submit to the OED Director written reports on a quarterly basis certifying: (1) compliance with the terms of his probation in the underlying criminal case or that his probation has been terminated; and (2) compliance with all directives of relevant healthcare professionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports are due at three months after the date the Final Order is signed, six months, nine months, etc.; these reports are affirmative certifications of compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause procedure for alleged probation noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes Respondent failed to comply during probation, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to Respondent's last address of record, and grant Respondent fifteen (15) days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If, after the 15-day response period and consideration of any response, the OED Director continues to believe there was noncompliance, the OED Director shall deliver the Order to Show Cause, Respondent's response (if any), and argument/evidence to the USPTO Director and request immediate suspension of up to an additional four months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-stay of suspension during review
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event the USPTO Director suspends Respondent pursuant to the Order to Show Cause and Respondent seeks a review of the suspension, any such review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any review or appeal does not automatically stay an additional suspension ordered by the USPTO Director under subparagraph f.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60 except as expressly addressed by the Agreement and the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order incorporates the regulatory duties for suspended practitioners, subject to specified exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to jurisdictions and administrative agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall provide notice of his suspension to all State and Federal jurisdictions and administrative agencies to which he is admitted to practice as set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(1)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal notification of suspension to other bars/authorities is required to fulfill § 11.58 duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to clients and arrangements for representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall provide notice of his suspension to all clients he represents having immediate or prospective business before the Office as set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(1)(ii); the notice need not be served by certified mail but may be served by electronic mail provided the email includes both a delivery receipt and a read receipt; and Respondent shall make appropriate arrangements for legal services to be rendered on behalf of his clients during the period of his suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows electronic service with delivery/read receipt in lieu of certified mail and requires practical steps to protect clients' interests while suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to opposing practitioners/parties in pending matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall provide notice of his suspension to the practitioners for all opposing parties (or to the parties in the absence of a practitioner representing the parties) in matters pending before the Office as set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(1)(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures opposing counsel/parties in pending USPTO proceedings are informed of the suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on holding oneself out as authorized to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not hold himself out as authorized to practice law before the Office as set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(3) until he is reinstated to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express prohibition during suspension against representing authority to practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to remove advertising or representations of authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall take any necessary and appropriate steps to remove from any telephone, legal, or other directory any advertisement, statement, or representation which would reasonably suggest that he is authorized to practice patent law as set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(1)(vi) until he is reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactive removal of public materials that could mislead about current authority to practice is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on rendering legal advice or services to clients with USPTO matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not render legal advice or services to any person having immediate or prospective business before the Office as set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(5) until he is reinstated to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute bar on providing representation on matters before the USPTO while suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disassociation of registration number from USPTO customer numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall disassociate his registration number from all active USPTO Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative step to prevent use of registration number during suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: 90-day exceptions to certain § 11.58 duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent does not have to comply with the following duties as a consequence of being suspended on the date of this Final Order unless a petition for reinstatement is not granted within 90 days of the Final Order: (1) file a notice of withdrawal in each pending application (§ 11.58(b)(1)(i)); (2) deliver to all clients the respective documents (§ 11.58(b)(1)(iv)); and (3) relinquish to the client, or another practitioner designated by the client, all funds for practice before the Office, including any legal fees paid in advance that have not been earned and any advanced costs not expended (§ 11.58(b)(1)(v)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporary relief from some immediate administrative duties for up to 90 days unless reinstatement petition is denied after that period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of compliance and required appendices
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall provide an affidavit of compliance in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(2), certifying that he has complied with the provisions of the Agreement and the Final Order. Appended to the affidavit shall be: (1) a copy of the forms of notice, the names and addresses of the clients, practitioners, courts, and agencies to which notices were sent, and all return receipts or return mail received up to the date of the affidavit as set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(2)(i); and (2) a list of all other State, Federal and administrative jurisdictions to which Respondent is admitted to practice as set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(2)(v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit serves as formal certification of compliance with notice and reporting duties and must include documentary proof of notices and a list of jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit exclusions (what need not be appended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's affidavit of compliance need not append: (1) a schedule showing the location, title, and account number of every bank account designated as a client or trust account, deposit account in the Office, or other fiduciary account, and of every account in which Respondent holds or held as of the entry date of the Final Order any client, trust, or fiduciary funds for practice before the Office (37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(2)(ii)); (2) a schedule describing Respondent's disposition of all client and fiduciary funds for practice before the Office in Respondent's possession, custody, or control as of the entry date of the Final Order or thereafter (37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(2)(iii)); or (3) proof of the proper distribution of funds and the closing of such accounts (37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(2)(iv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies documentary items that are not required to be appended to the affidavit of compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for reinstatement procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall file a petition for reinstatement as a condition of reinstatement; shall not resume practice until reinstated by order of the OED Director or USPTO Director as set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.60(a); any petition shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60(a), (b), and (c), including the fee required by 37 C.F.R. § 1.21(a)(10); and any petition shall attest to Respondent's compliance with the applicable provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 set forth in this Final Order, including a sworn declaration or affidavit that he has not engaged in the practice of patent law during his suspension, except as set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the OED Director receives a petition within 75 days of the Final Order, the OED Director shall not publish a notice of the petition as set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.60(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the provided notice text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final disciplinary actions are publicly posted; the Official Gazette notice summarizes the disposition and the misconduct basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order shall prevent the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct concerning Respondent or in any future disciplinary proceeding against Respondent as an aggravating factor or to rebut representations, and/or in connection with any request for reconsideration pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record may be used to aggravate future discipline or to rebut claims of mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of rights to reconsideration, review, and appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent waives all rights to seek reconsideration of the Final Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.56, waives the right to have the Final Order reviewed under 37 C.F.R. § 11.57, and waives the right otherwise to appeal or challenge the Final Order in any manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent voluntarily relinquishes procedural appellate rights as part of the settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party shall bear its own costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No award of costs between the parties as part of this settlement and Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating considerations in determining discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent represented: long registration (19 years), no prior professional discipline, age (61), no prior criminal history, restitution paid ($160,000 plus insurer payment), served 118 days confinement, compliance with criminal probation conditions, steps taken to ensure no similar misconduct will occur, compliance with healthcare directives, that misconduct resulted from isolated poor self-management, lack of intent to violate USPTO Rules, and expressed remorse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factual representations and circumstances are presented as mitigating facts considered in agreeing to and approving the sanction.
